chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated this hadith from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, Fudayl, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام.

The proper way regarding this narration and its conformity with the other narration is that we interpret it as indicating choice, and that a person has the option to act according to either one of them. However, acting upon the first narration is more apparent, and Zurarah, the narrator of this hadith, has indeed narrated something like the first report.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرِ: the principle of allowing a choice between two valid alternatives
key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ: the narration or report under discussion
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ الْأَوَّلِ: the first report mentioned for comparison and preference
key_terms.مُطَابَقَتِهَا: its correspondence or agreement with another report

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile differing narrations about Salat al-Khawf in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This passage discusses reconciling two narrations in the matter of Salat al-Khawf by carrying them upon takhyir, meaning that one may act upon either of the two reports. At the same time, it states that acting upon the first narration is more evident, and it supports this by noting that Zurarah also narrated a report similar to the first one.
